newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks ordered to detail non-performing loans.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks ordered to detail non-performing loans.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday said commercial banks and finance companies must detail their non-performing loans, effective in 1997.

The BOT said at a news conference that banks and finance companies would have to report non-performing loans, which had insufficient collateral, and which clients could not finance interest payments for more than six months.
Non-performing loans, with sufficient collateral, but which could not be serviced for more than 12 months would also have to be reported in detail to the central bank, it added.
In the past, banks and finance companies were not required to detail all non-performing loans to the central bank.
A large portion of current non-performing loans for banks and finance companies are believed by analysts to be in the depressed Thai property sector.
